2026-10-10T18:20:34.0113649Z # Subtest: release · A TOKEN IS SCOPED TO WHAT IT WRITES: the settings page states the minimum scope and why each part is needed
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0120629Z not ok 519 - release · A TOKEN IS SCOPED TO WHAT IT WRITES: the settings page states the minimum scope and why each part is needed
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0122168Z   ---
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0122807Z   duration_ms: 106.636737
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0123450Z   type: 'test'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0124898Z   location: '/home/runner/work/agent-m/agent-m/tests/release-sprint-01-dashboard-app.test.mjs:1094:1'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0126192Z   failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0126895Z   error: 'Contents with why'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0127543Z   code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0128188Z   name: 'AssertionError'
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0128786Z   expected:
2026-10-10T18:20:34.0145611Z   actual: " Step A · Create your key on GitHub Open GitHub's token page (prefilled) ↗ On that page: Under “Repository access”, choose “Only select repositories”. GitHub preselects “All repositories”, which would give Agent M write access to everything you own. Open “Select repositories” and pick “akmaier/agent-m” — nothing else. Leave the permissions as they are (Contents: read and write, Issues: read and write, Pull requests: read and write, Actions: read and write, Workflows: read and write, Metadata: read), scroll down and press “Generate token”. Copy the token GitHub now shows — it starts with github_pat_ and is shown only once. What is this? A token is a key you create on GitHub and give to this page, so it can make commits for you — only in the repositories you select, only with the permissions Agent M's features need, and only until the date you choose. You can delete it on GitHub at any time; it then stops working immediately. Why these permissions? Contents (read and write): to save and accept: every edit and acceptance is a commit you ask for by clicking; Issues (read and write): for reports that become issues in a product; Pull requests (read and write): for a job on GitHub's machines to open and merge its pull request; Actions (read and write): to start a run of a workflow, such as the tests; Workflows (read and write): for a job that writes a product's CI configuration, the files under .github/workflows/; Metadata (read): GitHub requires it for every token; it reads names and settings, nothing else. One key covers all of them. Each product you add later gets a key of its own. Why “Only select repositories”? GitHub preselects “All repositories”. That would let this page write to every repository you own. Choosing only the repository named above limits it to what Agent M actually needs. "

| release · A TOKEN IS SCOPED TO WHAT IT WRITES: the settings page states the minimum scope and why each part is needed |  | " Step A · Create your key on GitHub Open GitHub's token page (prefilled) ↗ On that page: Under “Repository access”, choose “Only select repositories”. GitHub preselects “All repositories”, which would give Agent M write access to everything you own. Open “Select repositories” and pick “akmaier/agent-m” — nothing else. Leave the permissions as they are (Contents: read and write, Issues: read and write, Pull requests: read and write, Actions: read and write, Workflows: read and write, Metadata: read), scroll down and press “Generate token”. Copy the token GitHub now shows — it starts with github_pat_ and is shown only once. What is this? A token is a key you create on GitHub and give to this page, so it can make commits for you — only in the repositories you select, only with the permissions Agent M's features need, and only until the date you choose. You can delete it on GitHub at any time; it then stops working immediately. Why these permissions? Contents (read and write): to save and accept: every edit and acceptance is a commit you ask for by clicking; Issues (read and write): for reports that become issues in a product; Pull requests (read and write): for a job on GitHub's machines to open and merge its pull request; Actions (read and write): to start a run of a workflow, such as the tests; Workflows (read and write): for a job that writes a product's CI configuration, the files under .github/workflows/; Metadata (read): GitHub requires it for every token; it reads names and settings, nothing else. One key covers all of them. Each product you add later gets a key of its own. Why “Only select repositories”? GitHub preselects “All repositories”. That would let this page write to every repository you own. Choosing only the repository named above limits it to what Agent M actually needs.
